Also, the story wasn't any of that 3deep5u bullshit Bioshock was trying to pull, and they just attempted to tell a decent story with what the setting allowed.

Bioshock was about showcasing graphical improvements, like with water, as well as attempting a more "mature" story with actual philosophical underpinnings. The architecture is very much art deco, meets underwater dreamscape, all with a tinge of decay. You may not have liked the story, but it was at least an attempt to tackle the Ayn Rand topics about individualism, and society, but oddly enough, without her level of subtly. The isolation is kind of a feature of the story in the first Bioshock. If you weren't digging the archetecture, the soundscape, the music, as well as not caring for the story, then yeah, you would find it boring. Infinite is a better game, weaker overall impact, just due to the competition before and after Bioshock. I personally think it irons out the complaints in the other two Bioshocks, but, the design, and story are obvious extensions of what was seen before, but it doesn't have the same level of "new" that the first Bioshock brought to the table.

Half-Life, both 1, and 2, are among the few groundbreaking games, and I don't think I have seen anyone even attempt to say Bioshock was better, or on the same level. But then again, I always considered Bioshock was a prettier, smoother game mechanics, dumbed down System Shock 2. But if you disliked the isolation in Bioshock ... as much as I love System Shock 2, maybe you should just try some other genres. But looking over the different systems of ranking "the greatest games ever", Bioshock is tied, or ranked higher then Half-Life consistently. So I guess I agree, I think the Bioshock games are overrated, but it is more about putting Bioshock in the "top 100 of all time" list personally as opposed to the "top 50 of all time".
